key_insight: A small set of real measurements can be used to validate a high-fidelity FEM model, then generate synthetic data to train a fast GNN surrogate for soft tactile deformation.
engineering_relevance: This enables millisecond-scale tactile deformation prediction for design exploration and real-time visualisation without needing large physical datasets or repeated sensor testing.
method: Use 82 camera-tracked contact cases to tune and validate an ANSYS FEM model.
Generate 768 synthetic contact scenarios from the validated FEM.
Train GNN surrogates for forward and inverse tactile deformation prediction.
evidence_signal: The validated FEM achieved sub-0.5 mm error in over 90% of validation cases, and the GNN reached 0.32 mm mean absolute error with millisecond inference.
watch_item: The demonstrated sim-to-real performance is limited to the tested planar 2D tactile structure, so broader geometries or loading conditions may need retraining or new validation.
paper_title: FEM-Validated Real-Time Modelling of Soft Tactile Deformation
